text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- The Great Belt company, building a bridge and tunnel link from the island of Zealand to the Danish mainland estimates that righting safety flaws discovered in a tunnel exercise last week will cost 50 to 100 million crowns.
---A survey of leading businesses shows that 22 percent established alliances with foreign partners in 1996 and another 48 percent expect to do so by the year 2,000.

---The government has finalised plans to toughen competition law punishing companies with turnover of more than 150 million crowns who abuse a dominant market position or attempt to limit competition.
--- Telecom group Tele Danmark could be hit by extensive strikes after its announcement on Wednesday that it intended to fire 2,500 staff by mid-1998.

--- Fur company Birger Christensen is to take over fur departments in the U.S.A's largest department store Macy's making it one of the world's largest furriers, with a global annual turnover of 625 million crowns.

--- The Schengen open border agreement between several European Union countries could be expensive for using Copenhagen Airport as they will have to pay the 450 million crowns that Copenhagen Airport is to invest in new passport control areas.
